_note: Authored foundations batch for the Government lessons that the audited 2020 paper does not cover: definition/scope, basic concepts, and forms/systems. Four questions per topic, each with a checked key and explanation.
subject: government

questions.question: Government is best defined as the institution that ______.

options.text: makes and enforces laws for a society
manages the profits of private businesses
interprets religious law for its members

questions.explanation: Government is the institution through which a state makes, enforces and interprets binding rules. Elections and private business are not its defining function.

questions.question: Which of the following is a function of government?

options.text: Fixing the career of every citizen

questions.explanation: Governments maintain law and order, defend the territory and provide public goods such as roads, schools and health care. They do not run every private company or choose personal careers and religions.

questions.question: The state differs from government because the state ______.

options.text: makes laws while the government does not

questions.explanation: The state is the permanent political community with territory, population, government and sovereignty. A government is the temporary machinery that runs the state and can be replaced.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a function of government?
questions.explanation: Maximising private profit is the aim of a private business, not a core function of government. Law and order, defence and public goods are government functions.

questions.question: Power is best defined as the ability to ______.

options.text: influence others even against their resistance

questions.explanation: Power is the capacity to affect the behaviour of others, including against resistance. Winning an election or interpreting the constitution are specific ways power may be acquired or exercised.

questions.question: Authority differs from power because authority is ______.
questions.explanation: Authority is legitimate power: those subject to it accept that the ruler has a right to command. Power alone may rest on force or wealth without that acceptance.

questions.question: The four elements of a state are territory, population, government and ______.
questions.explanation: A state needs a defined territory, a population, a government and sovereignty. Parties, a written constitution and an army are not defining elements.

questions.question: A nation is best described as ______.

options.text: a people sharing a common identity

questions.explanation: A nation is a group of people united by a shared identity, history or culture. A territory, a government or a constitution alone does not make a nation.

questions.question: In a parliamentary system, the executive is ______.

options.text: drawn from and answerable to the legislature

questions.explanation: In a parliamentary system the prime minister and cabinet come from the legislature and depend on its confidence. A separately elected executive is a feature of the presidential system.

questions.question: A system in which the president is both head of state and head of government is ______.
questions.explanation: In a presidential system the president combines the roles of head of state and head of government. In a parliamentary system the two roles are usually separate.

questions.question: Rule by a small group considered the best is called ______.
questions.explanation: Aristocracy is rule by a small group regarded as the best qualified. Democracy is rule by the people, autocracy is one-person rule and gerontocracy is rule by the elderly.

questions.question: A constitutional monarch ______.
questions.explanation: A constitutional monarch is a ceremonial head of state whose powers are limited by the constitution. An absolute monarch, by contrast, rules personally.
